steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Retrieval means finding information that is directly stated in the text. You don't need to guess or interpret - the answer is right there in black and white.

steps.title: Key idea 2
steps.body: Top Tips: Write in your own words where possible (but keep close to the text) You can use bullet points or numbered lists Each point should be a complete idea Don't repeat the same point in different words

steps.title: Examiner's Tip
steps.body: This is one of the easiest questions on the paper. Don't overthink it - just find four things and write them down. Aim to complete this in about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Retrieval Exam Strategy
steps.body: This is the easiest question on the paper - don't overcomplicate it. For AQA Paper 1 Q1 (4 marks), spend no more than 5 minutes. Read the question carefully, note any line references, scan for keywords, then write four clear points. For AQA Paper 2 Q1 (true/false), go back to the text and verify each option before choosing. Examiners mark this question generously - they want to give you full marks. Just find the information and state it clearly.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: When answering a "List four things" question, should you use your own words or copy the text exactly? | What's the difference between retrieval and inference? | How long should you spend on AQA Paper 1 Q1?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Write in your own words where possible (but keep close to the text) | You can use bullet points or numbered lists | Each point should be a complete idea

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Read the question carefully and check line references Don't analyse language - just find facts Use bullet points for clarity Check you have the right number of points Keep answers concise - don't waffle This is usually the easiest question - get it done quickly!
